Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM4348 : Measurements, Sensors, and Transducer { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Fundamentals of Measurement and Errors
SI Units: Fundamental and derived units, importance in measurement. Types of Errors: Systematic errors (instrumental, environmental, observational), random errors. Expression of Uncertainty: Accuracy and precision index, statistical treatment of uncertainty. Error Propagation: Uncertainty in addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Calibration and Standards: Traceability, national and international standards.
Module 2: Electrical Measurement Instruments
Analog Measuring Instruments: PMMC, MI, and Dynamometer-type instruments – working principles and applications. DC Potentiometer: Principles, applications, and standardization. Bridge Circuits: Wheatstone, Kelvin, Maxwell, Hay, Anderson, and Schering bridges for R, L, and C measurements. Q-Meter: Principle, construction, and applications in measuring quality factor. Digital Instruments: Digital voltmeter (DVM), digital multimeter (DMM), advantages over analog meters.
Module 3: Measurement of Electrical Quantities
Voltage, Current, and Power Measurement: Single-phase and three-phase circuits. True RMS Meters: Importance in measuring non-sinusoidal waveforms. Instrument Transformers: Current transformers (CT) and potential transformers (PT) – construction, working, and applications. Time, Phase, and Frequency Measurement: Timer/counter, phase meters, and frequency counters. Oscilloscope: CRO and DSO, signal visualization, bandwidth, and triggering techniques.
Module 4: Sensors and Transducers
Types of Sensors: Resistive, capacitive, inductive, piezoelectric, Hall effect
Signal Conditioning Circuits: Amplification, filtering, and conversion techniques. Industrial Transducers: Displacement (linear and angular), velocity, acceleration, force, torque, vibration, and shock sensors. Pressure and Flow Measurement: Low-pressure sensors, differential pressure, variable area, electromagnetic, ultrasonic, turbine, and open-channel flow meters. Temperature and Other Measurements: Thermocouples, bolometers, RTDs (3/4 wire), thermistors, pyrometers, semiconductor sensors, liquid level, pH, conductivity, and viscosity sensors.
Module 5: Biochemical Transducers and Biomedical Instrumentation
Electrode Theory: Principles of biopotential electrodes, electrochemical interactions. Biopotential Electrodes: Surface electrodes, needle electrodes, and applications in ECG, EEG, and EMG. Optical Sensors: Photodetectors, optical fiber sensors, fluorescence-based sensors. Indicator Mediated Transducers: Enzyme-based biosensors, biochemical analyte detection. Biomedical Recording Systems: Principles of ECG, EEG, and EMG recording electrodes, noise reduction, and biomedical signal processing.

Course Objective

1 .

To develop an understanding of the basic principles of measurements and measurement systems.
2 .

To understand the methods of measurement and errors associated with measurements.
3 .

To understand the basic principle of sensors & transducers and their classifications.
4 .

To understand the characteristics of different biosensors & transducers and their application in the biomedical field.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students will be able to understand the purpose and methods of measurements.
2. Students will be able to understand the use of different display, recording, and measuring devices for various applications.
3. Students will be able to understand the concepts, types, working and practical applications of sensors.
4. Students will be able to know the principle of transduction, classifications and the characteristics of different transducers.
5. Students will be able to choose a proper sensor and transducer based on their characteristics for measurement of different parameters related to biomedical applications.

Essential Reading

1 .

Richard S.C. Cobbold, Transducers for Biomedical Measurements: Principles and Applications, John Wiley & Sons

2 .

Harry N, Norton, Biomedical sensors – fundamentals and application, Harry N, Norton

Supplementary Reading

1 .

I. Sinclair, Sensors and Transducers: A Guide for Technicians, Newnes

2 .

T. R. Padmanabhan, Industrial Instrumentation: Principles and Design, Springer

6431.t: CE6136: Strength and Deformation Behaviour of Soil
6431.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6136 : Strength and Deformation Behaviour of Soil { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Physico-Chemical aspects, Failure theories, Yield criteria, Elastic and Plastic analysis of soil, Mohr’s diagram. Stresses in Soil: Description of state of stress and strain at a point, stress distribution problems in elastic half pace. Boussinessqu, Westergard Mindlin and Kelvin problems Distribution of contact pressure Analysis of Elastic settlement Soil Plasticity Shear Strength of Soils: Experimental determination of shear strength, Types of tests based on drainage conditions and their practical significance, Skempton’s and Henkel’s pore water pressure coefficients, Stress path, Shear strength of unsaturated soils, Row’s stress dilatancy theory. Constitutive Models: Constitutive Models in Soil Mechanics: Isotropic Elastic, Anisotropic Plasticity and Viscous Models. Representing Soil Behaviour using these Models Advances in Constitutive models.

Course Objective

1 .

Able to apply engineering knowledge.
2 .

Design/development of solutions for complex engineering. problems
3 .

Able to carry out investigations of complex problems.
4 .

Environment Impact and sustainable solution.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Learn the Physio-Chemical aspects, Failure theories, Yield criteria, Elastic and plastic analysis of soil.
2. Finding the stresses and strains in soil using Mohr's diagram and analysis of elastic settlement , soil plasticity, shear strength of soil.
3. Knowledge on the different constitutive models in soil mechanics and advances in each of these models.

Essential Reading

1 .

A.P.S. Selvadurai, Plasticity & Geomechanics, Cambridge University Press , Cambridge, UK

2 .

W.F. Chen, Limit Analysis & Soil Plasticity, Elsevier Scientific , Amsterdam, USA

Supplementary Reading

1 .

C. S. Desai and J. T. Christian, Numerical Methods in Geotechnical Engineering, McGrew Hill , New York, USA

2 .

R. F. Scott, Principles of Soil Mechanics, Addison & Wesley , Boston, UK

8223.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH1003 : Waves and Optics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Coordinator :

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: (7 hours)
Review of Simple Harmonic Motion, Damped and Forced oscillations, Resonance, coupled oscillations. Normal modes.
Module 2: (7 hours)
Wave Motion, wave equation, plane waves, phase velocity, superposition, wave packets and group velocity, dispersion relations.
Module 3: (10 hours)
Divergence and curl of static Electric & magnetic fields, Faraday’s law and Maxwell's correction for time dependent fields, Maxwell's equations in vacuum & media. EM waves & transverse nature of waves.
Module 4: (6 hours)
Coherence, superposition of waves, Interference, Two-beam and Multi-beam interference.
Module 5: (6 hours)
Fresnel Biprism, Newton’s rings, Michelson Interferometer, Thin films.

Course Objective

1 .

To learn independent and coupled oscillation processes such as springs, atoms, etc.
2 .

To learn the effect of damping on the oscillation process.
3 .

To learn wave motion and energy transmission.
4 .

To Formulate and analyze Maxwell’s equations in both vacuum and material media, emphasizing their physical significance.
5. To learn the basic optics phenomena such as coherence, superposition, interference, and their applications.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to:
CO1: Recognize and use mathematical oscillator equation and wave equation and derive these equations for certain systems.
CO2: Understand the effect of damping and periodic force on the oscillating body.
CO3: Understand the making of the Lissajous figures and the motion of coupled oscillators.
CO4: Understand the formulation of Maxwell’s equations in both vacuum and material media.
CO5: Use the principles of wave motion and superposition to explain the physics of interference.

Essential Reading

1 .

A. P. French, Vibrations and Waves: MIT Introductory Physics Series, CBS Publishers.

2 .

A. Ghatak, Optics, Tata-McGraw Hill.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

H. J. Pain, The Physics of Vibrations and Waves, Wiley (2005).

2 .

F. A. Jenkins and H. E. White, Fundamentals of Optics, Tata-McGraw Hill (2017).

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE3705 : Geotechnical Engineering Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Moisture Content of Soil and Specific Gravity of Fine-Grained and Coarse-Grained Soil [3 hours]
Module 2 :

Atterberg’s Limits (Liquid Limit, Plastic Limit, Shrinkage Limit) [3 hours]
Module 3 :

Grain Size Analysis (Mechanical Sieve Analysis and Wet Analysis) [3 hours]
Module 4 :

Field Density by Core Cutter Method and Sand Replacement Method [3 hours]
Module 5 :

Free Swell Index Test and Laboratory Vane Shear Test [3 hours]
Module 6 :

OMC and MDD Using (a) Light Compaction Test, (b) Proctor Needle Test [3 hours]
Module 7 :

Direct Shear Test and Laboratory Vane Shear Test [3 hours]
Module 8 :

Unconfined Compression Test and Triaxial Shear Test (UU) [3 hours]
Module 9 :

Permeability Tests (Constant Head and Falling Head) and pH Value of Soil [3 hours]
Module 10 :

California Bearing Ratio (CBR) Test: (a) Soaked, (b) Un-soaked [3 hours]
Module 11 :

Consolidation Test [3 hours]

Course Objective

1 .

Identify and classify different types of soils
2 .

Evaluation of compaction properties of soil
3 .

Evaluation of strength parameters of soil
4 .

Determination of permeability of soil

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, the students will be able to:
CO1: Determine and analyze the physical properties of soils, including moisture content, specific gravity, and Atterberg limits.
CO2: Conduct grain size analysis using mechanical sieve and wet analysis methods to classify soils.
CO3: Perform field density determination using core cutter and sand replacement methods to evaluate in-situ soil density and compaction.
CO4: Evaluate shear strength, compaction, and swelling characteristics of soil.
CO5: Assess unconfined compressive strength, permeability, and bearing value of soil.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC6509 : Satellite Communication { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1. Introduction and Orbital Dynamics: [6]
Overview of Satellite Communication, Historical background and current State, Kepler’s three laws of planetary motion, orbit of satellite, Orbital elements, look angle determination, Placement of GEO satellite, orbital perturbation and orbital effects on Communication System performance.
Module 2. Space and Ground Segment: [6]
Satellite subsystems: Attitude and orbit control system, Telemetry, Tracking, Commands and Monitoring, Power system, Communication system, Satellite antennas, Reliability. Equipment for the Earth station, Small earth station antennas.
Module 3. Satellite Link Budget: [8]
Basic transmission theory, system noise temperature and G/T ratio, down link design, up-link design, overall carrier-to-noise ratio (CNR), effect of interferences and atmospheric attenuation.
Module 4. Modulation and Multiple Access Techniques: [8]
Digital modulation techniques, Frequency division multiple access, time division multiple access, code division multiple access, practical demand access systems, random access, multiple access with on-board processing Satellite
Module 5. Advanced Satellite Systems: [8]
Applications of Satellite Communication, Small satellites, Satellite television, Satellite internet, Satellite navigation system.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand basic principle of satellite communication.
2 .

To gain practical knowledge of satellite communication for societal need.
3 .

To design and analyze the satellite link budget.
4 .

To study subsystems of satellite communication.

Course Outcome

1 .

After completion of this course students will be able to
1. Understand the concepts of satellite communication and orbital dynamics.
2. Gain knowledge of practical satellite communication systems including Navigation, satellite internet, satellite television.
3. Evaluate sub-systems including space and ground segments of satellite communication.
4. Design overall link and analyze satellite communication performance.
5. Apply link budget and communication techniques for advanced satellite Systems.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ME6202 : Machine Tool Technology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I [6 h]: General classification of machine tools: Making and Auxiliary motions, Hydraulic transmission and the elements, Mechanical Transmission and the elements. General requirements of machine tools, Copy Turing, Transfer machines. Kinematics of machine tools: Drives in Machine tools, Mechanical drives for providing rotational motions, Requirements for layout of stepped drive,
Module II [7 h]: Designing the layout of mechanical drive, Mechanical drive for reciprocation, Gear drive for feed motions, steeples drive. Strength and rigidity analysis of machine tool structures: Basic Principles of design for strength and rigidity, Optimum design criteria, state compliance of M/C tool, Design of lathe beds, Design of columns for pillar drill, Radial drill milling machine,
Module III [7 h]: Analysis and design of tailstock assembly. Guide ways and power screws: Classification of guide ways, Material and Lubrication, Design criteria and calculation for slide ways, Design of guides under hydrostatic lubrication, Aerostatic slide ways, Antifriction slide ways, Combination guide ways, Classifications of Power Jarms, Design Principles of power screw, Repower screw analysis.
Module IV [8 h]: Machine tool spindles and the Bearings: Materials of spindles, Effect of machine tool compliance or machining accuracy, Design principles of spindles, Antifriction and sliding bearing. Cold rolling system in machine tools: Classification, control system for charging speeds and feeds, Ergonomic considerations applied for design of control members, Principles of automatic and adaptive control.
Module V [8 h]: Vibration in Machine Tools: Sources and effects of vibration theory of chapter, Chapter in drilling, Milling and grinding, Elimination vibration, Stick-ship vibration and, Vibration.

Course Objective

1 .

Understand fundamental concepts in machine tool design
2 .

To know about various common techniques used in design of machine components
3 .

To be acquainted with different influencing factors, and the methods of controlling, the quality of products, in particular strength, rigidity and dimensional accuracy.
4 .

Relate theory of elasticity/plasticity to machine tool design

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Knowledge will be gained on design of machine components.
CO2: Able to apply the theory to practical problems.
CO3: Knowledge will be enhanced to implement the concept for product development.
CO4: Able to choose suitable attributes for component design
CO5: Able to determine safe force for operation
